svg.title: Four Decisions Before Committing Capital
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-wrap-preflight-decision-tree; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Decisions Before Committing Capital; subtitle: Each affirmative branch advances; each unresolved branch stops commitment.; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: The four nodes are sequential decision checks. Stage numbers represent order, not probabilities. Transaction scope, state requirements, lien terms, and borrower use determine the applicable rules; a servicer does not cure defective origination.; caption: Do not conceal a transfer, substitute a trust label for statutory analysis, or infer lender permission from continued payment acceptance. Keep written evidence for every decision.; stages: label: Can acceleration be absorbed?; value: Yes advances; absent funding means decline the acquisition; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Review 12 U.S.C. §1701j-3 and the actual due-on-sale clause. Document lender permission where obtained or specific statutory protection where applicable. Otherwise quantify payoff exposure and verify available liquidity or a credible refinance plan.; label: Is origination properly structured?; value: Yes advances; deficient underwriting returns to licensed RMLO; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Route every owner-occupant wrap buyer through a licensed RMLO. Map SAFE Act requirements under 12 U.S.C. §§5102–5103 and Regulation Z §§1026.36 and 1026.43. Document coverage, repayment capacity, compensation treatment, and any specifically applicable exemption.; label: Are state wrap requirements satisfied?; value: Yes advances; missing notices stop closing preparation; numeric value: 3.0; detail: For Texas, counsel checks Property Code §5.016 for covered encumbered-property conveyances, including applicable advance notices, and Finance Code Chapter 159 for wrap licensing and transaction duties. Document recipient, delivery timing, closing conditions, and applicable exceptions rather than copying generic forms.; label: Can title and payments remain controlled?; value: Yes permits closing; unresolved control defects require remediation; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Confirm lien priority, current taxes, insurance interests, and foreclosure remedies. Contract a licensed third-party servicer, document applicable Regulation X duties, test underlying-payment reporting, and fund transaction-specific reserves before accepting buyer funds.

circle.title: label: Can acceleration be absorbed?; value: Yes advances; absent funding means decline the acquisition; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Review 12 U.S.C. §1701j-3 and the actual due-on-sale clause. Document lender permission where obtained or specific statutory protection where applicable. Otherwise quantify payoff exposure and verify available liquidity or a credible refinance plan.

text.title: Review 12 U.S.C. §1701j-3 and the actual due-on-sale clause. Document lender permission where obtained or specific statutory protection where applicable. Otherwise quantify payoff exposure and verify available liquidity or a credible refinance plan.

circle.title: label: Is origination properly structured?; value: Yes advances; deficient underwriting returns to licensed RMLO; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Route every owner-occupant wrap buyer through a licensed RMLO. Map SAFE Act requirements under 12 U.S.C. §§5102–5103 and Regulation Z §§1026.36 and 1026.43. Document coverage, repayment capacity, compensation treatment, and any specifically applicable exemption.

text.title: Route every owner-occupant wrap buyer through a licensed RMLO. Map SAFE Act requirements under 12 U.S.C. §§5102–5103 and Regulation Z §§1026.36 and 1026.43. Document coverage, repayment capacity, compensation treatment, and any specifically applicable exemption.

circle.title: label: Are state wrap requirements satisfied?; value: Yes advances; missing notices stop closing preparation; numeric value: 3.0; detail: For Texas, counsel checks Property Code §5.016 for covered encumbered-property conveyances, including applicable advance notices, and Finance Code Chapter 159 for wrap licensing and transaction duties. Document recipient, delivery timing, closing conditions, and applicable exceptions rather than copying generic forms.

text.title: For Texas, counsel checks Property Code §5.016 for covered encumbered-property conveyances, including applicable advance notices, and Finance Code Chapter 159 for wrap licensing and transaction duties. Document recipient, delivery timing, closing conditions, and applicable exceptions rather than copying generic forms.

circle.title: label: Can title and payments remain controlled?; value: Yes permits closing; unresolved control defects require remediation; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Confirm lien priority, current taxes, insurance interests, and foreclosure remedies. Contract a licensed third-party servicer, document applicable Regulation X duties, test underlying-payment reporting, and fund transaction-specific reserves before accepting buyer funds.

text.title: Can title and payments remain controlled?

Confirm lien priority, current taxes, insurance interests, and foreclosure remedies. Contract a licensed third-party servicer, document applicable Regulation X duties, test underlying-payment reporting, and fund transaction-specific reserves before accepting buyer funds.

Assumptions: The four nodes are sequential decision checks. Stage numbers represent order, not probabilities. Transaction scope, state requirements, lien terms, and borrower use determine the applicable rules; a servicer does not cure defective origination.
